message.content:
For an unbiased (fair) coin each flip has two equally likely outcomes—heads or tails.  
Since there’s only one “head” outcome out of two possible outcomes:

\[
P(\text{Head})=\frac{\text{Number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{Total number of outcomes}}
               = \frac{1}{2}=0.5=50\%.
\]

So the probability of landing on heads in a single flip of a fair coin is **½** (or 50%).
